title: Killing innocents
hookLine: the Qur'an: whoever kills a soul unjustly, it's as if he killed all humanity (5:32)

cards: Two brothers, the sons of Adam, each bring an offering. One is accepted, one isn't. The one refused says, I will kill you.
The other answers, in the Qur'an's telling, that even if his brother reaches out a hand to kill him, he won't reach out his own. Then it happens anyway.
The killer doesn't even know what to do with the body, until a raven scratches at the ground and shows him. That's Surah al-Ma'idah. Straight after the grave comes the verse.

teach.h: NAFS: A HUMAN BEING, ANY HUMAN BEING.
teach.b: In Pickthall: "whosoever killeth a human being for other than manslaughter or corruption in the earth, it shall be as if he had killed all mankind, and whoso saveth the life of one, it shall be as if he had saved the life of all mankind."
Three things in that sentence. First, who. The Arabic word is nafs, a soul, a living person.
Not a believer, not a neighbor, not one of us. A human being. Second, the arithmetic.
One death counts as all of humanity. The verse refuses to let a single killing be small. And it runs the other way: save one life, and it's as if you saved everyone.
A paramedic, a lifeguard, a stranger who pulls someone back from the curb. Third, where it's set. The verse begins, for that cause, We decreed for the Children of Israel.
Placed right after the story of Adam's two sons, and given as a decree to an earlier people, it reaches back before Islam, to the family of Adam.
The hadith then draw lines even inside war.
In Sahih al-Bukhari, Ibn 'Umar reports that a woman was found killed after one of the Prophet's battles, and the Prophet Muhammad, peace be upon him, forbade the killing of women and children.
And in the Muwatta of Imam Malik, Abu Bakr sends an army out with orders: do not kill women, or children, or the old; do not cut down fruit trees. Even in war, there were lines.

how: Muslim scholars and preachers cite 5:32 when condemning attacks on civilians, and some mosques hold prayers for victims of violence, whoever they are.

o: a sin the Qur'an counts only when the victim is a Muslim
a wrong that is forgiven if it happens during a war

games.q: you're the brother whose offering was accepted. your brother says he will kill you. what do you say, in the Qur'an's telling?
o: even if you raise your hand to kill me, I won't raise mine to kill you.
games.why: he refuses to raise his hand. the killing happens anyway, and the verse on the worth of one life follows straight after.

practice: Bring to mind one place where people have been killed, in the news, in history, in your own city, and picture not the violence but one person who was there, someone's sister, someone's son, on an ordinary morning.
Hold them as a whole world, the way the verse counts them. If you pray, pray for them and those who grieve them, in your own words or the ones you usually use; if not, simply keep them in mind.

wordCard.voice: Killing innocents. In Surah al-Ma'idah, to kill one human being unjustly is as if killing all mankind; to save one is as if saving all. Today's word.

orig.note: Arabic: a soul, a living person; the word Pickthall renders 'a human being' in 5:32.

carryVoice: Your line: every soul sacred. No one is only a number. Go gently.
